stories.body: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro exchanged accusations of corruption and lying in their first debate before Brazil’s October 25 presidential runoff. Bolsonaro, who led the first round 47% to Lula’s 45%, focused on living costs and crime, while Lula challenged his spending-cut plans and highlighted Bolsonaro’s family ties to scandals and paramilitary groups.
stories.headline: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro trade attacks in Brazil runoff debate

stories.body: A large overnight Ukrainian drone attack killed at least one person, injured five others and caused fires at Saint Petersburg’s oil terminal and Ruchyi oil depot. A logistics centre and a VK data centre were also hit, while Russia said it had downed more than 1,000 drones nationwide. The attack followed Kyiv’s accusation that Moscow had repeatedly breached a US-backed pause on energy attacks.
stories.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Saint Petersburg oil facilities

stories.body: Donald Trump said his decision to suspend planned sanctions on Russia was intended to keep Moscow at the negotiating table over the war in Ukraine. Volodymyr Zelenskyy said easing sanctions would strengthen Russia’s war effort and warned against treating him and Vladimir Putin alike. The dispute follows a US deal to import Russian diesel and continued Russian and Ukrainian strikes on energy infrastructure.
stories.headline: Trump defends Russia sanctions pause amid strains with Ukraine

stories.body: Donald Trump gave Benjamin Netanyahu his “complete and total endorsement” nine days before Israel’s October 27 parliamentary election. Trump called the prime minister a strong and reliable ally, despite reports of disagreements between the two leaders over regional conflicts. Netanyahu’s Likud-led coalition faces a close contest against an opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot.
stories.headline: Trump endorses Netanyahu before Israel’s election

stories.body: Anthropic said it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund for public-benefit work, with the possibility of adding more equity as its value rises. The Claude maker said the fund could support nonprofits, direct payments to specific groups and work addressing AI’s effect on employment. It said the fund will not be used for political donations or lobbying.
stories.headline: Anthropic pledges 5% of its shares to a public-benefit fund

stories.body: Human Rights Watch reports that more than 320 people have been detained in Senegal since February amid an intensified crackdown on LGBTQ+ people, with at least 84 charged with voluntary HIV transmission solely because of their HIV status. The arrests follow legislation increasing penalties for same-sex relations and related advocacy. Lawyers and health workers say fear of prosecution is also deterring people from seeking legal help, HIV testing and treatment.
stories.headline: Senegal’s LGBTQ+ people face mass arrests and forced HIV testing

stories.body: Tejano musician Bobby Pulido is running as a Democrat against Republican Representative Monica De La Cruz in a closely watched South Texas House race. Pulido is pitching affordability, immigration and culturally conservative values to Latino voters in a district Donald Trump won by 18 points in 2024. Democrats see the campaign as a test of whether a moderate, locally rooted messenger can rebuild support among Mexican American voters.
stories.headline: Democrats test Tejano star Bobby Pulido’s appeal in South Texas

stories.body: Georgia Senator Raphael Warnock is raising money and recruiting donors for Democrat Scott Colom’s challenge to Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi. Warnock argues that Democrats have overlooked the South and its Black voters, though the party’s national groups have committed far more resources to other Senate races. Colom faces steep odds in a state Trump won by 24 points in 2024, but supporters hope stronger turnout and sustained organizing can make future gains possible.
stories.headline: Raphael Warnock pushes Democrats to invest in Mississippi Senate race

stories.body: Republican Senator Dan Sullivan is leaning into Donald Trump’s support as he faces a close reelection contest against former Representative Mary Peltola. Sullivan has avoided broad public breaks with Trump, including over the economic effects of the Iran war, while voicing concerns privately about US imports of Russian diesel. Peltola is campaigning on costs, local communities and independence from national party politics in a state where independents outnumber Republicans.
stories.headline: Dan Sullivan embraces Trump in tight Alaska Senate race

stories.body: Spain’s Constitutional Court is considering whether to hear an urgent appeal from the Ombudsman over the suspension of voting rights for more than 160,000 Spanish citizens abroad who obtained nationality under the Democratic Memory Law. The Supreme Court imposed the precautionary suspension following challenges by Vox and Iustitia Europa. Vox argues the appeal is premature because the Supreme Court is still accepting submissions from affected people until October 22.
stories.headline: Constitutional Court weighs action over voting rights under the grandchildren law

stories.body: The government is preparing a decree to expand protections for several groups as part of a series of pre-election measures. Proposed changes include temporary-incapacity coverage for menopause-related conditions, improved benefits for victims of gender violence, broader access to survivor pensions for unmarried couples with children, and stronger support for parents caring for children with cancer or serious illnesses.
stories.headline: Government plans benefit reforms before November election

stories.body: Ceuta’s public hospital has sent a court at least 20 medical reports from migrants who say they were injured by soldiers on patrol. The documents identify the alleged victims and describe their injuries, potentially giving the investigation evidence that earlier anonymous complaints lacked. The allegations follow a large-scale arrival of migrants in late July and reports by Amnesty International of possible mistreatment and torture.
stories.headline: Ceuta hospital provides injury reports in investigation of alleged military assaults

stories.body: The government aims to approve its electricity transmission plan through 2030 before the November 29 election. The plan would invest more than €17 billion and add 6,700 kilometres of network capacity to connect renewable generation, industry, technology projects and new housing. The government says the congressional permanent deputation can receive the plan while parliament is dissolved, clearing a legal uncertainty that had delayed the process.
stories.headline: Government moves to approve electricity-grid expansion before election

stories.body: Mossos d’Esquadra found more than 30 kilograms of copper and a transformer at a waste-management facility in Sant Martí that Adif specialists believe may have come from the railway network. The find came during inspections of three facilities, where authorities also identified administrative, labour and environmental violations. Separately, police recently arrested two people accused of stealing 134 kilograms of railway copper near La Sagrera.
stories.headline: Police investigate suspected stolen railway copper found in Sant Martí

stories.body: Barcelona has opened a tender for the design and construction management of 76 public housing units at Entença and Montnegre streets, part of the redevelopment of Colònia Castells in Les Corts. The wider project will combine the public homes with roughly 150 to 160 private units. The district expects to select the winning design team in January and lay the first stone around January 2028.
stories.headline: Barcelona tenders design for 76 public homes in Les Corts

stories.body: Adif expects to restore both tracks between Ricla and Plasencia de Jalón in Aragón on Monday, allowing the Barcelona–Madrid high-speed route to return to normal frequencies and journey times. A fire in the final part of a Renfe train a week earlier forced the closure of both tracks and caused days of delays and cancellations after service resumed on only one track.
stories.headline: Barcelona–Madrid high-speed line expected to return to full service

stories.body: Barcelona has 246 newcomer classrooms that provide recently arrived students with intensive Catalan instruction, basic knowledge and gradual entry into mainstream classes. At Institut Icària, staff say the programme also focuses on emotional support and social inclusion, helping students build confidence as they adapt to a new school and community.
stories.headline: Barcelona’s newcomer classrooms help recently arrived students settle in
